headline: Shai Hope's century powers West Indies to record 250-run chase against India, leveling series
summary: West Indies completed their highest successful T20I chase, overhauling a target of 250 against India in Ranchi, thanks to an unbeaten 102 from captain Shai Hope.
details: West Indies achieved their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a daunting target of 250 to defeat India by six wickets in Ranchi. This victory leveled the five-match series at 1-1.
Captain Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten century, scoring 102 runs off just 45 deliveries. This remarkable performance secured the win with nine balls to spare.
The chase began precariously for West Indies, with paceman Mayank Yadav removing Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer in successive deliveries. Rovman Powell also fell early for 24.
However, Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the tide with a blistering 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Rutherford capitalized on a dropped catch, smashing 84 runs off 37 balls.
This monumental chase stands as the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history. Only South Africa's pursuit of 259 against West Indies in 2023 surpasses it.
Earlier, India posted a formidable total of 249-5, largely thanks to Sanju Samson's 82 off 41 balls. He and Abhishek Sharma provided a strong opening partnership.
India accelerated at the death with Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma adding 83 runs from 32 balls. Iyer contributed 40 runs before falling on the penultimate delivery.
caption:
West Indies pulled off a historic 250-run chase against India in Ranchi, marking their highest successful T20I pursuit ever!

West Indies achieved their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a daunting target of 250 to defeat India by six wickets in Ranchi. This victory leveled the five-match series at 1-1.

Captain Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten century, scoring 102 runs off just 45 deliveries. This remarkable performance secured the win with nine balls to spare.

The chase began precariously for West Indies, with paceman Mayank Yadav removing Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer in successive deliveries. Rovman Powell also fell early for 24.

However, Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the tide with a blistering 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Rutherford capitalized on a dropped catch, smashing 84 runs off 37 balls.

This monumental chase stands as the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history. Only South Africa's pursuit of 259 against West Indies in 2023 surpasses it.

Earlier, India posted a formidable total of 249-5, largely thanks to Sanju Samson's 82 off 41 balls. He and Abhishek Sharma provided a strong opening partnership.

India accelerated at the death with Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma adding 83 runs from 32 balls. Iyer contributed 40 runs before falling on the penultimate delivery.

headline_marked: [[US imposes sanctions on ICC]] hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize, sparking diplomatic row
headline: US imposes sanctions on ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize, sparking diplomatic row
summary: The International Criminal Court denounced the move as an "assault on the rule of law," urging its 125 member states to defend the institution against Washington's actions.
details: The US President Donald Trump's administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday. This move came hours after one of its former judges, Navi Pillay, won the Nobel Peace Prize, putting Washington on a diplomatic collision course with European allies.

The ICC denounced the sanctions as an "assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order." It called on its 125 member states to take action to defend the court, stating that its fate now rests in their hands.

The Trump administration has long been hostile to the ICC, founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide. The US aims to prevent the court from prosecuting Americans, according to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Rubio stated that the US would ban transactions with the "rogue court," cutting off its resources and crippling its ability to operate. The Treasury announced the sanctions with an initial six-month grace period and some exemptions.

Washington has previously denounced the ICC over arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan. The ICC says the Afghanistan investigation is "deprioritized."

ICC Deputy Prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan told Reuters that the sanctions are intended to undermine international rule of law. She affirmed that the court's work would continue across all its situations, investigations, and prosecutions.

The Nobel Prize awarded to South African jurist Navi Pillay, who served on the ICC's Appeals Chamber from 2003-2008, was explicitly described as a gesture of support for such tribunals. The prize committee highlighted the importance of an international legal system for a peaceful world.

US sanctions typically bar all US-based companies from working with a sanctioned organization, forcing banks to shut accounts and insurers to end coverage. Court officials have been preparing for months, shifting software and making new arrangements for banking and health insurance.
